4 افلق He did, or performed, or he uttered, what was admirable, or wonderful; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) said of a man, (S, O, TA,) and (TA) of a poet, (S, * O, * Msb, K, TA,) in his poetry; (TA;) as also ↓ افتلق . (S, K.) [From فِلْقٌ, q, v.] ―
-b2- And He brought to pass that which was a calamity; (K;) as also ↓ افتلق . (Lh, TA.) One says to a man, أَعْلَقْتَ وَأَفْلَقْتَ i. e. جِئْتَ بِعُلَقَ فُلَقَ, meaning [Thou hast brought to pass] that which is a calamity. (S, O, K. *) ―
-b3- And افلق فِى الأمْرِ He was, or became, skilled in the affair. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
